You still don't need a plugin for this. There's no such thing as "word recognizing". With or without a plugin, you still have to connect "words" to "actions" yourself because no one else knows what you actually need.
What you can do without plugin if you need many different actions is:
Create one large common event (or a few connected ones)
Add all the needed actions inside it using conditional branches
Treat it like your own little "database" of word → action pairs
Then, when the player types a word in the input:
Save the input into a variable
Call that common event
Inside the common event → check the variable and see if it matches any of your conditions
This way your map event stays clean it usually contains just the text input + a call to the common event. You also get full control over your own word-matching and can create your own word correction logic(in common event too).
The plugin will pretty much do the same thing(checking matches) and you still have to write the words and actions yourself. There’s no way around it, the only difference is that it will be formatted as a plugin instead of a common event.
I think what you can ask the plugin for is a fancy input window with spell check I guess?

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
It's hard to think of things that are RPGMaker is missing that no-one else has done…
One line of thought is "extend event commands that only work in certain contexts", but I think most of these have been done?
Force get on/off vehicle even if not in the proper position (essentially, warp the vehicle next to the player before getting on, or disembark at a normally invalid location)
Does Character -> Show Animation work in battle? I don't remember.
Weather effects in battle -> already done by HimeWorks?
Change battleback in battle -> already done by HimeWorks?
Shop in battle -> I think I saw this somewhere but not sure
Name input processing in battle
Force Action on map (obviously actor only)
Self switches or This Event movement routes from common events? If I recall correctly, one of those works now and one of those doesn't. (Obviously, it can only possibly work when the common event is called by a map event.)
Such plugins wouldn't provide any commands or anything, just extend core event commands to work in more places.
Other small things that come to mind (but might have been done already):
Custom conditions on enemy action patterns (I
miiight
have seen this somewhere?)
Additional overlays for states
Additional weapon images - that is, extending the limit on how many can be used. (In fact, I don't think the engine enforces a limit on this anywhere – if the game were to ask for weapon 37, I think it would happily try to load Weapons4.png. But there's no way in the editor to ask for weapon 37.)

Parchment
. Then you can make the game-within-a-game separately using the proper software and just bundle it in. (And yes, you could totally bundle in Zork if you wanted to.)

ShadowDragon said:

Click to expand...
I use the vehicles for mechanics that are non-vehicular from the player perspective. For example, a "water walk" spell warps the boat in front of you and boards it, setting the boat image to the image of the party leader. Or a "flight" spell warps the airship to you and boards it, setting the airship image to the image of the spellcaster.
This takes a bit of scripting to get working, because "Get on/off vehicle" just simulates interacting with the vehicle – it only works if you're in position to get on or off.
Thus, I think a plugin command that bundles that logic up neatly would very helpful. Maybe multiple commands – "warp vehicle to player and board", and "disembark and warp vehicle to nowhere".
Actually, since I already got it working in one prototype game, I could make the plugin myself at some point; but I don't have plans currently to extract that logic into a plugin.

Click to expand...
The editor limits you to at most 10 SV state overlays and 30 SV weapon images in a given project. My prototype project has well over a hundred different states. Selecting only 10 of those to give a visual overlay isn't possible, and using the same overlay for quite different states is bound to be confusing. So I'd like to be able to use more than 10 overlays.
I'd be okay with either specifying a custom filename in the state note tag and using the normal dropdown to select a state from that sheet, or with making the existing file taller and indexing them with larger numbers. Whatever's more convenient.
A similar argument applies to SV weapons. In that case, the minimum I'd expect is something like this:
You can make Weapons3.png the size of Weapons2.png and put 6 more weapons in there.
There should be some way to specify that a certain weapon type uses an extended image (perhaps in the plugin parameters).
Bonus points for allowing to override the weapon image on specific weapons.
Note: I don't use Yanfly or VisuStella (except for a few of their simpler, free plugins), so even if they've done this before, I'd still like to see a non-VS version of it.

Allowing the player to swim is handled by the "summon vehicle" plugin. Swimming just means you enter the boat and change its image to the player's image. Of course, there could be more sophisticated ways of doing it, but this way is perfectly workable and can technically even be done without plugins (in fact, I think it can even be done without script calls, maybe).
I'd definitely like to know about plugins that add additional vehicles. For example:
A climbing vehicle that can move only on "ladder" terrains.
A rail cart that can only move on rail terrains.
A bus, car, truck, etc that can only move on road terrains.
